paragraphs: Baker, here's the big idea: when you look around for help, look to the LORD. The psalmist lifts his eyes to the hills and asks, "From where does my help come?" Then he answers it himself: "My help comes from the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth." (Psalm 121:1-2) The One who made the hills is the One you need, and that's a LOT more help than my rolling pin!

Now watch where the psalm goes next. It gets personal, from my to your, and it covers your feet, your days, your nights and your soul. "He will not allow your foot to slip; your Protector will not slumber." (Psalm 121:3) And that's not a tired helper who needs a nap, because "the Protector of Israel will neither slumber nor sleep." (Psalm 121:4) I can't even stay awake next to my own oven, so a Keeper who never dozes off? I LOVE that for you!

So what does this mean for your week, friend? It means the LORD is "the shade on your right hand," and "The LORD will guard you from all evil; He will preserve your soul." (Psalm 121:5, 7) It means the hard days and the long nights are not outside His watch. "The LORD will watch over your coming and going, both now and forevermore." (Psalm 121:8) So when you walk out the door tomorrow, you're not walking alone, and you can walk out with a smile.
